exercises.prompt: A controller does service.public_send(params[:operation]). It only uses public_send, so the author calls it safe. Repair the design.

trace.title: Class declaration
trace.detail: Metaprogramming means code that defines or changes program behavior, often methods. Rails uses it to build readable APIs. Start by locating the generated methods rather than assuming the behavior is unknowable.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
The class body runs as Ruby code. It iterates over LABELS and adds two instance methods. Calling done_label then uses normal method lookup. No generated source string is needed.

For a Rails concern or DSL, ask four questions: when does this declaration run, which object is self, which methods get defined, and which hooks are registered? Trace one declaration all the way to a runtime call.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: The books contain historical patterns such as alias_method_chain and old security assumptions. They are reading exercises, not a recommendation for new code. Rails 4.2 uses classic autoloading; modern Zeitwerk advice is a separate version topic.
